messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding run for 'sparrow-lite-v2-ptq' showed a small but consistent uptick in funcall JSON parse failures when the model is behind batching (especially mixed-seq batches). Repro attached below. Anyone else seeing this?
eric: I saw similar. Quick repro (local canary):
```bash
# curl to canary endpoint, streaming mode
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CANARY' -d '{"model":"sparrow-lite-v2-ptq","inputs":"call_tool: summarize(doc) -> {name:string,score:float}"}' https://canary.api.redwood/run
```
Output snippet:
```json
{"event":"partial","text":"{\"name\": \"AutoReport\", \"score\": 0.92,}\n"}
{"event":"partial","text":"}\n"}
```
(note the trailing comma + fragmented close)
joan: That looks like a streaming boundary + tokenization artifact plus PTQ-induced tokenization shifts. Could be the int8 quantization nudging EOS token placement, causing premature termination of the JSON object in some streams.
kgomez: Also noticed retries interact poorly: when the client retries a streaming request we sometimes get concatenated partials without a clear delimiter, e.g. `...}\n{\"name\":` which breaks most strict JSON parsers.
deploy-bot: Deployed sparrow-lite-v2-ptq -> infra/canary (revision r2026-ptq-3) at 2026-03-21T10:02:10Z
maya: Action plan proposal: 1) bisect runtime path (tokenizer vs kv-cache vs batching). 2) run flat float16 vs PTQ int8 w/ batching disabled. 3) run a 5k-call canary with streaming off (non-chunked) to measure parse failure rate. Thoughts?
eric: I'll run #2 and #3 today. Quick local numbers: with batching ON (batch-size=8) int8 parse failures ~1.8% on our sample; float16 ~0.03%. With batching OFF int8 drops to ~0.1%.
joan: That strongly implicates batching multiplexing. Could be interleaved KV cache offsets/resets when requests share a micro-batch. Maybe a race where decoder state for short sequences isn't zeroed quickly after a cached prefix.
kgomez: Also saw evidence that our JSON-rescue heuristic (strip trailing commas) _reduces_ visible failures but hides the real signal. We should not ship heuristic masking before root-cause.
maya: Agreed. But for product stability we might need a temporary post-process that logs and alerts on rescued JSONs while we fix the root cause. Logging should include the raw stream (hashed) + model revision + batch metadata.
eric: Repro logs (sanitized):
```
[10:15:12] batch_id=7 seq=3 model=sparrow-lite-v2-ptq tokens=64 partial='{"name": "AutoReport", "score": 0.92,'
[10:15:12] batch_id=7 seq=3 partial='}'
[10:15:12] parse_error: UnexpectedToken at EOF
```
joan: Proposed experiment: run three canaries in parallel for 24h: (A) PTQ int8 + batching, (B) PTQ int8 + batching disabled, (C) float16 + batching. Collect per-request: parse_ok(boolean), bytes_streamed, last_token, batch_size, kv-prefix-length.
sre-oncall: I'll reserve a small dedicated pool for the canary windows and add a trace hook to capture the last 256 bytes of the stream payload. Need exact times.
maya: Let's start windows at 2026-03-22T02:00Z for 6h each (staggered). Eric, can you own the test jobs? Joan, can you add the extra trace fields and the post-process that flags rescued JSONs (as soft-warning only)? kgomez, please prepare a small fuzz harness that injects retry/double-stream scenarios.
ergic: (typo) meant eric: ack, I'll kick off experiments and post results in this thread.
joan: One more note — if it's batching reordering, a long-term fix may be to tag streaming fragments with a per-request nonce in the envelope so parsers can detect cross-request merges instead of trying to infer from content. That is non-trivial but safer than heuristic JSON repair.
maya: Good idea. For now, keep heuristics out of mainline. Use them in A/B canary with explicit logging. We'll reconvene with numbers tomorrow. :thumbsup:
